Description

The Schedule has a display switch called Business Hours. It is meant to grey out the parts of the day the shop is not open, so that a planner can see at a glance which part of the row is real working time and which part is the middle of the night.

The switch does nothing you can see. With it turned on, the whole timeline from midnight through to eleven at night is the same flat white as the working day, so a shift placed at three in the morning looks exactly as normal as one placed at ten in the morning.

It matters because this is the only cue on the board that tells a planner where the working day begins and ends. Without it, out-of-hours work is invisible until somebody notices the time and questions it, and the switch itself looks broken because turning it on and off changes nothing on screen.

Branch / Environment

  • Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
  • API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
  • Build marker (<meta name="app-version">): v3.5-7ec992f
  • index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980
  • Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
  • Location / workplace: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
  • Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
  • Observed: 2026-08-06, 03:0x UTC

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in as a user who can view the schedule (an Administrator is fine) and pick the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  2. Open Schedule from the top navigation.
  3. Switch to Day view using the Day / Week / Month control, and go to Thursday, 6 August 2026. Any day behaves the same way; the fault does not depend on the date or on any particular work order, technician or shift, and no test data is needed to see it.
  4. Open the FILTER & DISPLAY dropdown in the toolbar and find the Business Hours switch. It is already on, which is its default.
  5. Look along the timeline from 12 AM through to 11 PM.
  6. Turn the Business Hours switch off, look again, then turn it back on and look a third time.

Expected behaviour

With the switch on, the hours outside the working day should be covered by a grey overlay so they are visibly different from the working part of the day.

The Schedule specification asks for exactly that, in two places:

"With the toggle on, the hours OUTSIDE the working day are shaded with a grey overlay."

Governing requirement: Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, section 9 (Business Hours) and section 4.8 (Business-hours shading).

Current behaviour

  • With the switch ON, the timeline from 12 AM to 11 PM renders uniformly white. Nothing is shaded, tinted or bordered.
  • With the switch OFF, the timeline looks identical.
  • With the switch turned back ON, the timeline still looks identical.
  • The only shaded element anywhere in the calendar in all three states is the divider between the department groups, which is unrelated to the time of day.

Images

No screenshot is attached. The finding was taken by reading the rendered page directly and was confirmed on a screen capture at the time, and the check is a single glance at the timeline, so an image adds nothing a reader cannot see immediately by following the steps.

Technical details for developers

Measured with the toggle ON, OFF and restored to ON. In each of the three states the count of elements carrying the shaded cell class was the same:

  • Elements matching fc-cell-shaded: 2 in all three states. Both are the resource-timeline divider (class fc-resource-timeline-divider fc-cell-shaded), which separates the department groups; neither is a time-of-day overlay.
  • No element in the Day-view time grid carries any non-working-hours class, background tint or overlay in any of the three states.
  • Confirmed visually on the captured screenshot, not only by class name.

This is not the same as the two nearby reports, and a duplicate search was run before filing:

  • SV-8827 Open is about the switch's DEFAULT STATE (it starts on when it should start off). This report is about the switch having no visible effect at all, whichever way it is set.
  • SV-8837 Open and SV-8915 Open are about where the view is scrolled to when it opens. This report is about the shading of the hours once you are looking at them.

comments.body:
Withdrawing this ticket - it was raised in error.

This was reported by us. It says the Business Hours switch shades nothing in Day view. That is not right, and the reason is our own mistake: the test case it came from starts with a precondition that says "The shop has working hours set", and when we looked at the screen the shop had no business hours set at all. The switch on the location screen was off, so there were no opening or closing times for the schedule to work from. With nothing set, there are no out-of-hours to shade, so shading nothing was the correct thing for it to do.

Re-checked today with the shop's hours actually set, and it works correctly.

The shop hours were set to 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, and the same Day view was looked at again on build v3.5-7ec992f:

  • With Business Hours turned OFF, nothing is shaded at all.
  • With it turned ON, two shaded bands appear - one covering midnight to 6 AM, and one covering 6 PM to midnight. The working day itself, 6 AM to 6 PM, is left clear.
  • Turning it off again removes the shading. This was repeated and behaved the same way each time.

The shaded band starts at exactly the 6 PM mark on the timeline, which is the shop's closing time, so it is shading the right hours and not simply shading something.

The test case behind this now passes, so nothing needs to be fixed.

Closing this rather than deleting it, so the reasoning stays on the record for anyone who looks at it later.
